q: The queen's speech had a profound ___ on everyone.
explain: Have an impact on = have a strong effect on. Example: The film had an impact on me.

notes.affect: Affect is a verb; we need a noun.
notes.result: A result doesn't go with 'on everyone'.

q: After months of practice, her efforts finally paid ___.
explain: Pay off = bring success. Example: All that training paid off.

notes.up: Pay up = pay money you owe.

q: The evidence was ___; nobody could argue with it.
explain: Overwhelming = very strong, too much to resist. Example: an overwhelming victory.

notes.overdone: Overdone = cooked too long or exaggerated.
notes.overcome: Overcome is a verb: overcome a problem.

q: We need to ___ the pros and cons before deciding.
explain: Weigh up = think carefully about. Example: Weigh up your choices.

notes.look up: Look up = find in a book or online.
notes.bring up: Bring up = mention or raise a child.

q: He's ___ to win — he's the best by far.
explain: Bound to = certain to. Example: It's bound to rain.

notes.liable: Liable to = likely to do something bad.
notes.prone: Prone to = often affected by (illness, mistakes).
notes.keen: Keen to = wants to, not certain.

q: Swimming is ___ prohibited in the north lake.
explain: Strictly prohibited = completely forbidden (a fixed phrase). Example: Smoking is strictly prohibited.

notes.strongly: Strongly goes with recommend or believe.

q: The new rules will come into ___ next month.
explain: Come into force = start to apply (laws). Example: The law came into force in May.

notes.power: Come into power is for governments.
notes.practice: Put into practice is the phrase with practice.
notes.play: Come into play = start to matter.

q: She ___ out of the competition due to injury.
explain: Pull out = withdraw. Example: He pulled out of the race.

notes.broke: Break out = escape or start suddenly.
notes.gave: Give out = stop working or hand out.

q: I can't ___ the difference between the two crystals.
explain: Tell the difference = see what's different. Example: I can't tell the twins apart.

notes.say: Say the difference isn't the phrase.
notes.know: Know the difference means understand it, not notice it.

q: The manager ___ the blame for the mistake.
explain: Take the blame = accept responsibility. Example: She took the blame.

notes.put: Put the blame on = blame someone else.

q: There has been a sharp ___ in the number of visitors.
explain: A rise (noun) = an increase. Example: a rise in prices.

notes.raise: Raise is mostly a verb (raise your hand).
notes.rouse: Rouse is a verb = wake up.

q: He has a reputation ___ being honest.
explain: A reputation for. Example: a reputation for kindness.

notes.of: Of isn't used with reputation like this.

q: Her explanation was ___; I understood instantly.
explain: Crystal clear = very easy to understand. Example: The rules were crystal clear.

q: We managed to ___ the problem by working together.
explain: Overcome = defeat a difficulty. Example: She overcame her fear.

q: He's very ___; he always finishes what he starts.
explain: Determined (adjective) = won't give up. Example: a determined climber.

q: Which word is the opposite of 'reluctant'?
explain: Reluctant = not wanting to; willing = happy to. Example: She was willing to help.

notes.unwilling: Unwilling means the same as reluctant.

q: Let's try to ___ a compromise.
explain: Reach a compromise / agreement. Example: They reached an agreement.

notes.arrive: Arrive needs 'at': arrive at a compromise.
notes.get: Get a compromise isn't the usual phrase.

q: The new bridge will ___ traffic in the town centre.
explain: Ease traffic = make it less heavy. Example: Medicine eased the pain.

notes.lighten: Lighten is for loads or colours.
notes.soften: Soften is for materials or attitudes.
notes.loosen: Loosen is for knots or belts.

q: Despite the setbacks, the team ___ to finish on time.
explain: Manage to + verb = succeed in something hard. Example: I managed to finish.

notes.achieved: Achieve takes a noun: achieve a goal.

q: Her argument was so ___ that everyone agreed.
explain: Compelling = very convincing. Example: compelling evidence.

notes.competing: Competing = trying to win against others.

q: We'll need to ___ costs if we want to stay in business.
explain: Cut back on = reduce. Example: Cut back on sugar.

notes.cut out of: Cut out of isn't used with costs.
notes.cut up with: Cut up with isn't a phrase here.

q: He's a ___ reader; he finishes a book every two days.
explain: A keen reader = loves reading. Example: a keen gardener.

notes.strong: Strong isn't used with reader this way.
notes.heavy: Heavy reader isn't the phrase (heavy eater is).

q: Visits to the tower are ___ appointment only.
explain: By appointment = only if you book. Example: Open by appointment.

q: The decision was made ___ consultation with local residents.
explain: In consultation with = after discussing with. Example: in consultation with teachers.

q: She was ___ with the job of organising the festival.
explain: Entrusted with = given an important job. Example: entrusted with the keys.

notes.entitled: Entitled to = have a right to.

q: His performance ___ all our expectations.
explain: Exceed expectations = be better than expected. Example: The trip exceeded our hopes.

notes.excelled: Excel = be very good at (no object like this).

q: It's ___ that she'll accept; she seemed very keen.
explain: Highly likely = very probable (collocation). Example: It's highly likely to snow.

q: The company has ___ a new policy on remote working.
explain: Adopt a policy = start using it. Example: The school adopted new rules.

q: Which word means 'to make something less serious or painful'?
explain: Alleviate = make less painful. Example: Rest alleviates tiredness.

notes.allocate: Allocate = give out for a purpose.

q: The two reports are ___ different; you can't compare them.
explain: An adverb (fundamentally) describes the adjective 'different'. Example: completely different.

notes.fundamental: Fundamental is an adjective; we need an adverb.
notes.fundamentalist: Fundamentalist is a person or belief.

q: They ___ a heated argument about money.
explain: Get into an argument = start one. Example: They got into trouble.

q: The astronauts had to ___ the mission because of a fuel leak.
explain: Call off = cancel. Example: They called off the match.

notes.call up: Call up = phone, or pick someone for a team.
notes.call in: Call in = visit briefly, or ask an expert to come.

q: I can't ___ how this puzzle works. It's too tricky.
explain: Figure out = understand after thinking. Example: I figured out the answer.

notes.figure in: Figure in = include in a calculation.
notes.look up: Look up = find in a book or online.

q: Our class ___ a brilliant idea for the charity fair.
explain: Come up with = think of an idea. Example: She came up with a plan.

notes.came down with: Come down with = start to have an illness.
notes.came round to: Come round to = finally agree with.

q: I ___ an old photo of my grandpa while tidying the attic.
explain: Come across = find by chance. Example: I came across a rare stamp.

notes.came up with: Come up with = think of an idea.
notes.came along: Come along = go somewhere with someone.

q: Don't ___ on your dreams just because one test went badly.
explain: Give up (on) = stop trying. Example: Never give up!

notes.give in: Give in = finally agree after arguing.
notes.give out: Give out = hand to many people.
notes.give away: Give away = give for free, or reveal a secret.

q: After hours of begging, Mum finally ___ and let us get a puppy.
explain: Give in = stop resisting and agree. Example: He gave in to the pressure.

notes.gave off: Give off = produce a smell or light.

q: Volcanoes ___ huge clouds of gas and ash.
explain: Give off = produce (smell, heat, light, gas). Example: The flowers gave off a sweet smell.

notes.give out: Give out = hand out to many people.

q: The detective promised to ___ the mystery of the missing trophy.
explain: Look into = investigate. Example: The police are looking into it.

notes.look down on: Look down on = think you're better than.
notes.look forward to: Look forward to = be excited about something coming.

q: Younger players really ___ the team captain.
explain: Look up to = admire and respect. Example: I look up to my sister.

notes.look out for: Look out for = watch carefully for.

q: I can't ___ with all this noise! I'm trying to study.
explain: Put up with = tolerate. Example: I can't put up with his jokes.

notes.put down: Put down = place on a surface, or criticise.

q: We need to ___ ideas for the school magazine.
explain: Bring up = mention a topic. Example: She brought up an interesting point.

notes.bring about: Bring about = cause something to happen.
notes.bring back: Bring back = return, or make you remember.
notes.bring round: Bring round = wake someone up, or persuade.

q: The new phones ___ big changes in how teens talk to each other.
explain: Bring about = cause to happen. Example: The storm brought about floods.

notes.brought up: Bring up = mention, or raise a child.
notes.brought on: Bring on = cause something bad, like an illness.

q: The band will ___ a new album next month.
explain: Bring out = release (a product). Example: They're bringing out a new game.

q: The school plans to ___ a new rule about phones.
explain: Bring in = introduce (a law or rule). Example: They brought in a new uniform.

notes.bring off: Bring off = succeed at something difficult.

q: The rocket ___ smoothly at dawn.
explain: Take off = leave the ground (a plane or rocket). Example: The plane took off late.

notes.took on: Take on = accept work, or employ.

q: She ___ too many clubs and now she has no free time.
explain: Take on = accept work or responsibility. Example: Don't take on too much.

notes.took off: Take off = remove, or leave the ground.
notes.took after: Take after = be like a parent.

q: The lesson was so fast that I couldn't ___ it all.
explain: Take in = understand and remember. Example: It was a lot to take in.

q: We ___ at dawn to climb the mountain.
explain: Set off = start a journey. Example: We set off early.

notes.set in: Set in = begin and continue (bad weather).

q: Winter ___ early this year, and the lake froze in November.
explain: Set in = start and probably continue (weather, a feeling). Example: Boredom set in.

notes.set out: Set out = start a journey with a goal.
notes.set about: Set about = start doing a task.

q: Losing the instructions ___ our robot project by a week.
explain: Set back = delay progress. Example: The injury set him back.

notes.set off: Set off = start a journey, or make an alarm ring.

q: The two friends ___ after an argument about a game.
explain: Fall out (with) = stop being friends after an argument. Example: They fell out over money.

notes.fell through: Fall through = fail to happen (a plan).
notes.fell for: Fall for = be tricked by, or fall in love with.

q: Our holiday plans ___ when the hotel closed.
explain: Fall through = a plan fails and doesn't happen. Example: The deal fell through.

notes.fell over: Fall over = trip and fall down.

q: I was ill for a week and ___ with my schoolwork.
explain: Fall behind = not keep up. Example: Don't fall behind with homework.

notes.fell for: Fall for = be tricked, or fall in love.
notes.fell back: Fall back = move backwards, or rely on.

q: I can't believe you ___ that silly prank!
explain: Fall for = be tricked by. Example: Everyone fell for the April Fool's joke.

q: We need to ___ a plan before the treasure hunt starts.
explain: Draw up = prepare a plan or list. Example: We drew up a timetable.

notes.draw on: Draw on = use knowledge or experience.

q: Can you ___ the music? I can't hear the film.
explain: Turn down = make quieter (or refuse). Example: Turn the TV down.

notes.turn up: Turn up would make it louder.

q: The mysterious stranger ___ to be our new teacher!
explain: Turn out = be discovered to be. Example: It turned out to be easy.

q: I'm ___ this weekend! I can finally sleep in.
explain: Look forward to = be excited about. Example: I look forward to seeing you.

q: The scientist ___ her theory with lots of evidence.
explain: Back up = support (an idea, with evidence). Example: Can you back up your claim?

notes.backed down: Back down = stop arguing and accept defeat.
notes.backed out: Back out = stop being part of a plan.

q: He promised to help with the play but ___ at the last minute.
explain: Back out = withdraw from an agreement. Example: She backed out of the deal.

notes.backed down: Back down = admit you were wrong.

q: Our class ___ a survey about favourite pets.
explain: Carry out = do (research, a survey, an experiment). Example: We carried out an experiment.

q: The heavy rain ___ serious damage to the garden.
explain: Cause damage. You can also say 'do damage'. Example: The storm caused damage.

q: I always ___ my best in tests.
explain: Do your best. Example: Just do your best.

notes.make: We don't say make your best.
notes.give: Give your best is possible in sport, but do your best is the fixed phrase.
notes.take: We don't say take your best.

q: You have to ___ the rules, or you'll be sent off.
explain: Obey / follow the rules. Example: Players must obey the referee.

notes.follow up: Follow up = do more about something later.
notes.keep up: Keep up = continue, or stay level.
notes.hold: We don't say hold the rules.

q: Can you ___ a secret?
explain: Keep a secret. Example: She can't keep a secret.

notes.hold: We don't say hold a secret.
notes.save: We don't say save a secret.
notes.take: We don't say take a secret.

q: We ___ a great time at the theme park.
explain: Have a good/great time. Example: Have fun!

notes.made: We don't say made a great time.
notes.did: We don't say did a great time.
notes.spent: Spend time, but not spend a great time.

q: He ___ a promise to help me, and he kept it.
explain: Make a promise. Example: I made a promise.

notes.did: We don't say did a promise.
notes.gave out: Give out = hand to many people.
notes.took: We don't say took a promise.

q: She ___ a speech at the end-of-year assembly.
explain: Give (or make) a speech. Example: The head gave a speech.

notes.told: Tell is used with stories and jokes.

q: I ___ a joke and everyone laughed.
explain: Tell a joke / story / lie. Example: Tell me a story.

notes.said: We don't say said a joke.

q: Our team ___ a lot of progress this term.
explain: Make progress. Example: You've made great progress.

q: Let's ___ a break and get some snacks.
explain: Take a break. Example: Take a five-minute break.

notes.make: We don't say make a break here.
notes.do: We don't say do a break.
notes.give: Give is used for 'give me a break' (stop annoying me).

q: I ___ an effort to talk to the new student.
explain: Make an effort. Example: Make an effort to listen.

notes.did: We don't say did an effort.
notes.took: We don't say took an effort.
notes.had: We don't say had an effort.

q: The heavy rain was a ___ blow to our picnic plans.
explain: A major blow = a serious setback. Example: The injury was a major blow.

notes.large: Large is about size, not a setback.

q: There was ___ rain all night, and the river flooded.
explain: Heavy rain / snow / traffic. Example: Heavy snow closed the school.

notes.strong: Strong goes with wind, not rain.
notes.hard: Hard rain is less natural than heavy rain.

q: There was a ___ wind, so the kites flew really high.
explain: Strong wind. Example: A strong wind blew the door shut.

notes.heavy: Heavy goes with rain, not wind.
notes.powerful: Powerful wind is possible but less usual than strong.

q: We couldn't see the path because of the ___ fog.
explain: Thick fog. Example: Thick fog delayed the plane.

notes.heavy: Heavy goes with rain and snow.

q: The ___ of the light bulb changed the world.
explain: Verb + -ion → noun for the thing. Example: discover → discovery.

q: She's very ___. She always has new ideas for stories.
explain: Imaginative = good at thinking of new ideas. Example: an imaginative writer.

notes.imaginary: Imaginary = not real: an imaginary friend.

q: My little brother has an ___ friend called Zog.
explain: Imaginary = existing only in your mind. Example: an imaginary world.

notes.imagined: Imagined is a past form, less natural here.

q: The ___ of the comet surprised scientists.
explain: Appear → appearance (noun). Example: His sudden appearance.

q: It's ___ to swim in the river after a storm.
explain: Danger → dangerous (adjective). Example: a dangerous road.

notes.endangered: Endangered = at risk of dying out.

q: Pandas are an ___ species.
explain: Endangered = at risk of disappearing. Example: endangered tigers.

q: The team showed great ___ when they were losing.
explain: Determine → determination (noun). Example: her determination to win.

q: The story was ___. I didn't believe a word of it.
explain: un- + believable = impossible to believe. Example: an unbelievable excuse.

notes.disbelieving: Disbelieving describes the person who doesn't believe.

q: It's ___ to talk loudly in the library.
explain: The negative of appropriate is inappropriate. Example: an inappropriate joke.

q: I ___ with you. I think cats are better than dogs!
explain: dis- + agree = disagree. Example: We disagree about films.

q: I ___ the instructions and built the model upside down.
explain: mis- = wrongly. Example: misspell, misread.

q: The robot was ___ in helping the old lady cross the road.
explain: -ful = full of. Example: careful, useful.

notes.helpless: Helpless = not able to help yourself.
notes.helping: Helping is a verb form or noun.

q: Without its shell, the snail was totally ___.
explain: -less = without. Example: homeless, fearless.

q: The magician performed his tricks ___.
explain: Adjective + -ly → adverb (how). Example: carefully, quickly.

q: The ___ of the game is to collect all the stars.
explain: The aim of = the purpose. Example: The aim is to win.

notes.end: The end is when it finishes, not its purpose.
notes.finish: The finish is the last part of a race.
notes.result: The result is what happens at the end, not the purpose.

q: Eating vegetables ___ your health.
explain: Affect is a verb; effect is a noun. Example: Sleep affects your mood.

notes.effects: Effect is usually a noun: a good effect.
notes.reflects: Reflect = send back light, or think deeply.

q: Sugar has a bad ___ on your teeth.
explain: Effect (noun) on. Example: The film had a big effect on me.

q: The magician's trick was so ___ that we gasped.
explain: -ive adjective describes the thing. Example: an impressive goal.

q: I'm ___ in learning about volcanoes.
explain: -ed adjective = how you feel. Example: I'm bored.

notes.interest: Interest is a noun or verb.

q: Please be ___ not to wake the baby.
explain: Careful = paying attention to avoid harm. Example: Be careful on the stairs.

q: We ___ the competition, so we got a medal.
explain: Win a competition. Example: She won the race.

notes.beat: You beat a person or team.

q: The ___ of the class is twenty-eight students.
explain: Size of a group. Example: the size of the room.

notes.measure: Measure is a verb or tool.

q: I didn't ___ that the test was today!
explain: Realise = become aware of a fact. Example: I realised I was late.

notes.recognise: Recognise = know someone/something you've seen before.

q: I didn't ___ my old friend; she'd grown so tall!
explain: Recognise = know who someone is when you see them. Example: I recognised her voice.

notes.realise: Realise is for facts, not faces.

q: The robot can ___ the stairs on its own.
explain: Climb = go up using feet/hands. Example: climb a tree.

notes.rise: Rise = go up by itself; it isn't used with an object.

q: If you know the answer, ___ your hand.
explain: Raise + object (lift up). Example: Raise your hand.

notes.rise: Rise has no object: The sun rises.

q: The sun ___ in the east.
explain: Rise (no object) = go up. Example: Prices rise.

q: Can you ___ me how to do this sum?
explain: Show someone how to do something. Example: Show me how it works.

notes.explain: Explain needs to: explain to me.
notes.say: Say doesn't take a person directly.
notes.learn: Learn is what the student does.

q: Don't worry about the test. It'll be a piece of ___.
explain: A piece of cake = very easy. Example: The quiz was a piece of cake.

notes.bread: Bread isn't part of this idiom.
notes.pie: Pie is in 'easy as pie', not 'a piece of'.
notes.toast: Toast isn't part of this idiom.

q: I'm feeling a bit under the ___. I think I've got a cold.
explain: Under the weather = slightly ill. Example: She's under the weather today.

notes.rain: Rain isn't part of this idiom.
notes.clouds: Clouds isn't part of this idiom.
notes.sky: Sky isn't part of this idiom.

q: We were all in the same ___: nobody knew the answer.
explain: In the same boat = in the same difficult situation. Example: We're all in the same boat.

notes.ship: Ship isn't used in this idiom.
notes.car: Car isn't used in this idiom.
notes.house: House isn't used in this idiom.

q: I'll keep my fingers ___ for your audition!
explain: Keep your fingers crossed = hope for good luck. Example: Fingers crossed it's sunny!

notes.closed: Closed isn't used in this idiom.
notes.tight: Tight isn't used in this idiom.
notes.folded: Folded isn't used in this idiom.

q: When I saw the spider, my heart was in my ___.
explain: Heart in your mouth = very scared or nervous. Example: My heart was in my mouth on the ride.

notes.hand: Hand isn't used in this idiom.
notes.throat: Throat isn't used in this idiom.
notes.head: Head isn't used in this idiom.

q: It was a ___ in the dark, but my guess was right!
explain: A shot in the dark = a complete guess. Example: My answer was a shot in the dark.

notes.step: Step in the dark isn't the idiom.
notes.jump: Jump in the dark isn't the idiom.
notes.walk: Walk in the dark isn't the idiom.

q: Ollie spilled the ___ about the surprise party.
explain: Spill the beans = tell a secret. Example: Who spilled the beans?

notes.peas: Peas isn't part of this idiom.
notes.milk: Milk isn't part of this idiom.
notes.secrets: Secrets is the meaning, not the idiom's word.

q: You hit the ___ on the head! That's exactly the problem.
explain: Hit the nail on the head = say exactly the right thing. Example: You've hit the nail on the head.

notes.hammer: The hammer hits the nail; it isn't the object.
notes.point: Point isn't used in this idiom.
notes.spot: Spot is in 'hit the spot' (be just right), a different idiom.

q: Getting up at 5 a.m. is not my cup of ___.
explain: Not my cup of tea = not something I like. Example: Horror films aren't my cup of tea.

notes.coffee: Coffee isn't used in this idiom.
notes.milk: Milk isn't used in this idiom.
notes.juice: Juice isn't used in this idiom.

q: I've been so busy that I'm ___ the clock.
explain: Race against the clock = hurry to finish before a deadline. Example: We raced against the clock.

notes.looking at: Look at the clock just means check the time.

q: The joke went over my ___. I didn't get it.
explain: Go over your head = be too difficult to understand. Example: The science talk went over my head.

notes.hair: Hair isn't used in this idiom.
notes.face: Face isn't used in this idiom.
notes.ears: Ears isn't used in this idiom.

q: Learning to juggle is easier said than ___.
explain: Easier said than done = harder than it sounds. Example: Waking up early is easier said than done.

notes.made: Made isn't part of this idiom.
notes.tried: Tried isn't part of this idiom.
notes.learnt: Learnt isn't part of this idiom.

q: We missed the bus, and to ___ it all, it started raining.
explain: To top it all (off) = and the worst thing was… Example: To top it all, I lost my keys.

notes.cap off: Cap off isn't used in this phrase.
notes.end: End isn't used in this phrase.
notes.finish: Finish isn't used in this phrase.

q: My grandma is seventy but still as fit as a ___.
explain: As fit as a fiddle = very healthy. Example: He's as fit as a fiddle.

notes.fish: Fish isn't used in this simile.
notes.horse: Horse is in 'eat like a horse', a different idiom.
notes.flower: Flower isn't used in this simile.

q: The new student was a fish out of ___ on her first day.
explain: A fish out of water = someone who feels uncomfortable in a new place. Example: I felt like a fish out of water.

notes.sea: Sea isn't used in this idiom.
notes.river: River isn't used in this idiom.
notes.tank: Tank isn't used in this idiom.

q: I had to bite my ___ to stop myself laughing.
explain: Bite your tongue = stop yourself saying something. Example: I bit my tongue and said nothing.

notes.lip: Bite your lip is similar but used for holding back feelings, not words.

q: Stop beating about the ___ and tell me what happened!
explain: Beat about the bush = avoid saying something directly. Example: Don't beat about the bush.

notes.tree: Tree isn't used in this idiom.
notes.garden: Garden isn't used in this idiom.
notes.field: Field isn't used in this idiom.

q: My grandma adores her puppy. He's the apple of her ___.
explain: The apple of someone's eye = the person or pet they love most. Example: The baby is the apple of his eye.

notes.heart: Heart isn't used in this idiom.
notes.face: Face isn't used in this idiom.
notes.hand: Hand isn't used in this idiom.

q: Gaming all night was a real ___ of time.
explain: A waste of time = time used for nothing useful. Example: That meeting was a waste of time.

q: Spell the word: to make a problem less serious
explain: A cold drink can ease a sore throat.

q: Spell the word: a person who owns or runs a business
explain: The young entrepreneur sells her own phone cases.

q: Spell the word: able to bend easily without breaking
explain: Gymnasts are very flexible.

q: Spell the word: to make something impossible or difficult
explain: The fog hindered the rescue team.

q: Spell the word: happening every year
explain: The annual school fair is in June.

q: Spell the word: the ability to keep going even when things are hard
explain: Learning the violin takes perseverance.

q: Spell the word: easy to see or understand
explain: The answer was obvious once she explained it.

q: Spell the word: to look at something carefully to find out more
explain: The vet examined the dog's paw.

q: Spell the word: the surroundings where people, animals and plants live
explain: We must protect the environment.

q: Spell the word: a feeling of not being sure
explain: I have no doubt she'll win.

q: Spell the word: extremely tired
explain: After the exams I felt completely drained.

q: Spell the word: to give help, money or time for free
explain: We volunteer at the animal shelter.

q: Spell the word: a strong wish to know or learn something
explain: Her curiosity led her to open the old box.

q: Spell the word: polite and kind to people
explain: It was considerate of you to wait for me.

q: Spell the word: to think that something is true without proof
explain: Don't assume the test will be easy.

q: Spell the word: a small amount of something
explain: Only a fraction of the cake was left.

q: Spell the word: not willing to change your mind
explain: My little brother is so stubborn!

q: Spell the word: to say you will definitely do something
explain: I promise I'll be back by six.

q: Spell the word: the feeling of being proud of yourself
explain: She felt a lot of pride after the race.

q: Spell the word: an amount that is more than enough
explain: There is plenty of food for everyone.

q: Spell the word: to change something slightly to improve it
explain: Adjust your seat before you start.

q: Spell the word: a person who is very good at something
explain: She's an expert on dinosaurs.

q: Spell the word: to give a reason for something you did
explain: Can you justify your answer?
